# BR-500 Control Narrative: pH and Dissolved Oxygen Control

**Document section:** 5.x pH and DO Control
**Equipment:** BR-500, 2000 L single-use CHO bioreactor
**Control system:** Emerson DeltaV, ISA-88 batch
**Status:** DRAFT. Values marked **[TBC]** are proposed and need confirmation by Process Engineering and QA before approval.

---

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This section defines the required behaviour of pH and dissolved oxygen (DO) control for BR-500. Each requirement has a unique ID (e.g. `PH-012`) and is written to be individually testable during OQ. Section 10 lists the open items that must be resolved before the document is approved.

**In scope:** pH measurement and probe selection, CO₂ and base addition, the base volume limit, DO measurement and probe selection, the DO cascade (agitation, air, O₂), phase-dependent enablement, setpoint management and audit trail.

**Out of scope:** temperature, pressure, level/weight, feeds, overlay gas, foam control, and probe calibration procedures. Interactions with these are noted where relevant.

## 2. Tag List

| Tag | Description | Range / Units |
|---|---|---|
| AT-501A / AT-501B | pH probes A / B | 2–12 pH [TBC] |
| AIC-501 | pH controller (control module) | pH |
| FCV-510 | CO₂ sparge mass flow controller | 0–2 slpm |
| P-520 | 1 M Na₂CO₃ base addition pump | [TBC: variable speed or pulsed] |
| WT-521 | Base bag load cell | kg |
| AT-502A / AT-502B | DO probes A / B | 0–200 % air sat. [TBC] |
| AIC-502 | DO controller (control module) | % air sat. |
| SIC-530 | Agitator speed controller | rpm |
| FCV-511 | Air sparge mass flow controller | 0–10 slpm |
| FCV-512 | O₂ sparge mass flow controller | 0–5 slpm |

## 3. General Requirements

### 3.1 Phase Enablement

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| GEN-001 | pH control (AIC-501) and DO control (AIC-502) shall be **active only** during the Equilibrate, Inoculate and Production phases. |
| GEN-002 | At the start of Equilibrate, the phase logic shall download the pH and DO setpoints from the recipe and place AIC-501 and AIC-502 in AUTO. SIC-530, FCV-510, FCV-511, FCV-512 and P-520 shall be placed in CAS. |
| GEN-003 | During Media Fill, AIC-501 and AIC-502 shall be in MAN with outputs at the inactive state defined in Table 3-1. Operator mode changes to AUTO/CAS shall be rejected (or the controllers shall be locked by the phase) [TBC: lock mechanism]. |
| GEN-004 | At the transition from Production to Harvest, AIC-501 and AIC-502 shall be set to MAN and the final elements driven to the inactive state in Table 3-1. |
| GEN-005 | If a phase in the active range (Equilibrate–Production) goes to HELD, pH and DO control shall **continue** at the current setpoints. Control is not suspended on hold. [TBC: confirm with Process] |
| GEN-006 | If a phase in the active range is STOPPED or ABORTED, control shall [TBC: continue in AUTO until operator action / go to inactive state]. Proposed: continue control, and annunciate a HIGH-priority alarm "BR-500 batch aborted, pH/DO control running outside batch." |
| GEN-007 | Control continues uninterrupted across the Equilibrate → Inoculate → Production transitions. No bump in final element output shall occur at a transition, unless the recipe setpoint changes. |

**Table 3-1: Inactive state of final elements**

| Element | Inactive state |
|---|---|
| FCV-510 CO₂ | 0 slpm |
| P-520 base | Stopped |
| FCV-512 O₂ | 0 slpm |
| FCV-511 air | 0 slpm [TBC: Harvest may require a minimum air flow] |
| SIC-530 | Released to phase control (setpoint defined by the Media Fill/Harvest phase, outside this section) |

### 3.2 Setpoint Management and Audit Trail

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| GEN-010 | Operator-entered setpoints shall be clamped to these limits: pH 6.50–7.50 [TBC], DO 10–80 % [TBC]. Entries outside the limits shall be rejected with a message, not silently clamped. |
| GEN-011 | During **Production**, any operator change to the pH setpoint, the pH deadband or the DO setpoint shall require entry of a **reason** before the change is accepted. A blank reason shall be rejected. [TBC: does "setpoint" also cover alarm limits, cascade limits and mode changes? QA to confirm.] |
| GEN-012 | Each setpoint change in GEN-011 shall be recorded in the DeltaV Event Chronicle **and** the batch record with: user ID, date/time, tag/parameter, old value, new value, reason, and batch ID. |
| GEN-013 | If the operator cancels the reason dialog, the setpoint shall remain at its previous value. |
| GEN-014 | Setpoint changes during Equilibrate and Inoculate shall be recorded in the Event Chronicle (user, time, old and new value). A reason is not required. [TBC: QA to confirm] |
| GEN-015 | Setpoint changes shall require the user to hold the "Supervisor" (or equivalent) privilege [TBC]. Operators without this privilege shall be unable to change the setpoint. |
| GEN-016 | Setpoint changes made by the batch recipe (phase logic) are recorded by the batch executive and do not require an operator reason. |

---

## 4. pH Measurement and Probe Selection

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-001 | A probe is **healthy** when all three are true: (a) its DeltaV status is GOOD; (b) its value is within 6.00–8.00 pH [TBC]; (c) it is not flagged out-of-service by the operator. |
| PH-002 | When both probes are healthy and their absolute difference is ≤ 0.10 pH [TBC], the control PV shall be the **arithmetic average** of AT-501A and AT-501B. |
| PH-003 | If only one probe is healthy, the control PV shall automatically switch to the healthy probe. A MEDIUM alarm "pH probe A/B failed, controlling on single probe" shall be raised. |
| PH-004 | If both probes are healthy but differ by > 0.10 pH [TBC] for > 60 s [TBC], a HIGH alarm "pH probe deviation" shall be raised. The PV shall remain the average until the operator selects a probe (A, B or AVG) from the faceplate [TBC: alternative is to hold outputs]. The operator selection shall be audit-trailed. |
| PH-005 | If no probe is healthy, the PV status shall go BAD. AIC-501 shall shed to MAN, FCV-510 shall go to 0 slpm, P-520 shall stop, and a HIGH alarm "pH measurement lost, control suspended" shall be raised. |
| PH-006 | When a failed probe returns to healthy, it shall **not** automatically rejoin the average. The operator shall re-enable it from the faceplate (audit-trailed). This prevents a bumpless-transfer upset from a probe that is still drifting. [TBC] |
| PH-007 | The faceplate shall display AT-501A, AT-501B, their difference, the selected PV, and the selection mode (AVG / A / B). |

## 5. pH Control

### 5.1 Control Strategy

The pH is controlled by a split-range strategy with a deadband around the setpoint:

- **Acid side (pH above the band):** CO₂ sparge via FCV-510. Added CO₂ forms carbonic acid and lowers pH.
- **Base side (pH below the band):** 1 M Na₂CO₃ via P-520 raises pH.

**Deadband interpretation [TBC]:** "Deadband 0.05" is taken here as **±0.05 pH** about the setpoint, giving a band of 6.95–7.05 at SP = 7.00. If it is meant as a total band width (6.975–7.025), the values below must be changed.

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-010 | Default setpoint 7.00 pH and default deadband 0.05 pH. Both are recipe parameters. |
| PH-011 | When PV > SP + DB, the acid side (FCV-510) shall act. The base pump shall be stopped. |
| PH-012 | When PV < SP − DB, the base side (P-520) shall act. FCV-510 shall be at 0 slpm. |
| PH-013 | When SP − DB ≤ PV ≤ SP + DB, P-520 shall be stopped and FCV-510 shall [TBC: ramp to 0 slpm / hold its last value]. Proposed: hold the last value, which is standard DeltaV deadband behaviour. Process to confirm. |
| PH-014 | CO₂ and base shall **never be added simultaneously**. This shall be enforced in logic independently of the controller output, so it holds in all modes, including MAN. |
| PH-015 | FCV-510 output shall be limited to 0–2 slpm. Values outside this range shall be rejected or clamped. |
| PH-016 | Base delivery shall be [TBC: pump speed proportional to controller output, 0–X mL/min / pulse-on time within a fixed cycle of X s]. |
| PH-017 | Controller tuning (gain, reset, rate) is defined in the tuning sheet [ref TBC]. It is not an OQ acceptance criterion; it is verified during PQ/engineering runs. |

### 5.2 Base Addition Limit (40 L per batch)

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| PH-020 | At the start of Equilibrate, the system shall capture the WT-521 weight as the **base reference weight** and reset the base-added totalizer to 0 L. |
| PH-021 | Base volume added (L) = (reference weight − current weight) ÷ base density. Density = 1.10 kg/L [TBC: confirm for 1 M Na₂CO₃ at storage temperature]. The value shall be displayed on the faceplate and historized. |
| PH-022 | When base added ≥ 36 L (90 %) [TBC], a MEDIUM alarm "Base addition approaching batch limit" shall be raised. |
| PH-023 | When base added ≥ 39.5 L [TBC: 40 L minus a margin for pump overrun and in-line volume], P-520 shall stop and be **interlocked off** for the remainder of the batch. A HIGH alarm "Base batch limit reached, base addition disabled" shall be raised. |
| PH-024 | The interlock in PH-023 shall act regardless of AIC-501 mode and P-520 mode, including manual pump commands from the operator. |
| PH-025 | After PH-023 trips, acid-side control (CO₂) shall continue normally. |
| PH-026 | The base limit interlock shall not be resettable by operators during the batch. Reset occurs only when a new batch reaches Equilibrate (PH-020). [TBC: QA to define whether a supervisor override with e-signature is allowed.] |
| PH-027 | If WT-521 status goes BAD, P-520 shall stop and be inhibited, and a HIGH alarm "Base weight lost, base addition inhibited" shall be raised. The system cannot prove the limit is respected without weight. |
| PH-028 | If the WT-521 weight increases by > 0.5 kg [TBC] while P-520 is running or stopped (bag change, bag touched, tare error), a HIGH alarm shall be raised and P-520 inhibited until a supervisor confirms. Base added shall **not** decrease as a result. The totalizer shall be monotonic, so the 40 L limit cannot be bypassed by a bag swap. [TBC: define the bag-change procedure] |
| PH-029 | The total base added at the end of Production shall be recorded in the batch report. |

### 5.3 pH Alarms

| ID | Alarm | Limit [TBC] | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| PH-030 | pH PV high | > 7.20 for 5 min | HIGH |
| PH-031 | pH PV low | < 6.80 for 5 min | HIGH |
| PH-032 | pH probe deviation | See PH-004 | HIGH |
| PH-033 | CO₂ flow deviation (FCV-510 PV vs SP) | > 0.2 slpm for 60 s | MEDIUM |
| PH-034 | Base pump fault (P-520 run feedback mismatch) | 5 s | HIGH |

Alarms PH-030/031 shall be active only in Equilibrate–Production, and shall be suppressed for 30 min [TBC] after Equilibrate starts to allow probes and media to stabilise.

---

## 6. DO Measurement and Probe Selection

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DO-001 | Probe health, averaging, single-probe fallback, deviation alarm, total loss and re-enable shall follow the same logic as PH-001 to PH-007, with these values [TBC]: valid range 0–150 %, deviation threshold 10 % air sat. for 60 s. |
| DO-002 | On total loss of DO measurement, AIC-502 shall shed to MAN and **hold the last outputs** (agitation, air, O₂). The pH-side fail-safe of going to zero is not used, because loss of oxygen supply harms the culture. A HIGH alarm "DO measurement lost, cascade frozen" shall be raised. [TBC: confirm with Process] |

## 7. DO Control

### 7.1 Cascade Strategy

AIC-502 is a single PID controller with output 0–100 %. Its output is split into three sequential ranges. Each range drives one actuator, and an actuator moves only when the one before it is at its maximum.

| Stage | AIC-502 output | Actuator | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 – 33.3 % [TBC] | SIC-530 setpoint | 80 → 140 rpm (linear) |
| 2 | 33.3 – 66.7 % [TBC] | FCV-511 air setpoint | 0 → 10 slpm (linear) |
| 3 | 66.7 – 100 % | FCV-512 O₂ setpoint | 0 → 5 slpm (linear) |

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| DO-010 | Default DO setpoint 40 % air saturation (recipe parameter). |
| DO-011 | While DO control is active, agitation shall be no lower than 80 rpm and no higher than 140 rpm, in all AIC-502 modes. |
| DO-012 | Air flow shall be > 0 slpm only when SIC-530 setpoint = 140 rpm. |
| DO-013 | O₂ flow shall be > 0 slpm only when SIC-530 setpoint = 140 rpm **and** FCV-511 setpoint = 10 slpm. |
| DO-014 | On decreasing demand, the stages shall unwind in reverse order: O₂ to 0, then air to 0, then agitation to 80 rpm. |
| DO-015 | The mapping between AIC-502 output and each actuator setpoint shall be linear within its stage. At the boundaries listed in the table above, the deviation shall be ≤ 1 % of span. |
| DO-016 | If SIC-530 is not in CAS (e.g. the operator has put it in AUTO or MAN), the cascade shall not advance to stage 2. AIC-502 shall be held at the stage 1 upper limit (anti-windup) and a MEDIUM alarm "DO cascade broken, agitator not in CAS" shall be raised. The same rule applies to FCV-511 when advancing to stage 3. |
| DO-017 | Air and O₂ flows shall be limited to 0–10 slpm and 0–5 slpm respectively, in all modes. |
| DO-018 | AIC-502 shall have anti-reset-windup when all three stages are saturated (100 %), and also when the output is at 0 % (80 rpm, no gas). |
| DO-019 | Controller tuning is per the tuning sheet [ref TBC] and is not an OQ acceptance criterion. |

### 7.2 DO Alarms

| ID | Alarm | Limit [TBC] | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| DO-030 | DO PV low | < 20 % for 5 min | HIGH |
| DO-031 | DO PV high | > 80 % for 10 min | MEDIUM |
| DO-032 | DO cascade at maximum (AIC-502 output ≥ 99 %) | 15 min | HIGH |
| DO-033 | Air / O₂ flow deviation | > 10 % of span for 60 s | MEDIUM |
| DO-034 | Agitator speed deviation (SIC-530 PV vs SP) | > 5 rpm for 30 s | HIGH |
| DO-035 | DO probe deviation | See DO-001 | HIGH |

Alarm suppression after Equilibrate starts shall be as for pH (30 min [TBC]).

---

## 8. Loop Interactions (informative, not OQ-tested)

- **Air and O₂ sparge strip CO₂.** This raises pH, which can increase base demand. A high-DO-demand culture therefore consumes the base budget faster. The 40 L limit (PH-023) is the guard against this.
- **CO₂ sparge adds gas volume and lowers DO partial pressure slightly.** The DO loop compensates for this.
- **Total sparge flow** (CO₂ + air + O₂, maximum 17 slpm) must stay within the bag and exhaust filter rating [TBC: confirm against the bag supplier's specification]. If the rating is lower, a total-flow limit must be added as a requirement.

## 9. OQ Test Derivation Guide

Each ID in Sections 3–7 maps to at least one OQ test case. These are suggested approaches:

| Requirement group | Suggested OQ method |
|---|---|
| GEN-001 to GEN-007 | Run a batch through each phase in simulation or a water batch. At each transition, verify controller modes and final element states. Hold and abort the phases. |
| GEN-010 to GEN-016 | Attempt setpoint changes within and outside the limits, in each phase, with and without a reason, and with privileged and non-privileged users. Verify the Event Chronicle and batch record entries field by field. |
| PH-001 to PH-007, DO-001/002 | Simulate probe values and status (BAD, out of range, deviation) using DeltaV simulate or a mA source. Verify PV selection, alarms and controller response. |
| PH-010 to PH-016 | Drive the simulated pH PV above, inside and below the band. Verify which actuator is active. Force both outputs in MAN to verify PH-014. |
| PH-020 to PH-029 | Simulate the WT-521 weight decreasing through the 36 L and 39.5 L equivalents. Attempt manual pump starts after the trip. Simulate a BAD load cell and a weight increase (bag change). Verify the totalizer never decreases. |
| DO-010 to DO-018 | Ramp the AIC-502 output in MAN from 0 to 100 % and back. Record all three actuator setpoints at the breakpoints. Break the cascade by changing SIC-530 or FCV-511 mode. |
| Alarms | Drive each condition across its limit, and verify the delay, priority, message text and suppression window. |

Tuning and control performance (settling time, overshoot) are verified in PQ/engineering runs, not in OQ.

## 10. Open Items (must be closed before approval)

| # | Item | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Deadband interpretation: ±0.05 or a total band width of 0.05 | Process |
| 2 | CO₂ behaviour inside the deadband: hold last value or go to 0 (PH-013) | Process |
| 3 | P-520 drive type and flow range (PH-016) | Engineering |
| 4 | Na₂CO₃ density, and the trip margin below 40 L (PH-021, PH-023) | Process / Eng. |
| 5 | Bag-change procedure, and whether a supervisor override of the base limit is permitted (PH-026, PH-028) | QA / Process |
| 6 | Probe deviation response: keep averaging or hold outputs (PH-004) | Process |
| 7 | Scope of "setpoint" for the reason requirement: alarm limits, deadband, cascade limits, modes (GEN-011) | QA |
| 8 | Setpoint privilege level and whether an e-signature (vs. a reason only) is required under Part 11 (GEN-015) | QA |
| 9 | Behaviour on HOLD and ABORT (GEN-005, GEN-006) and on DO measurement loss (DO-002) | Process |
| 10 | DO cascade breakpoints, and the total sparge-flow limit against the bag rating | Process / Eng. |
| 11 | All alarm limits, delays and suppression windows | Process / QA |
| 12 | Air flow requirement during Harvest (Table 3-1) | Process |

---

A note on approach: wherever the brief left a gap, I proposed a concrete value or behaviour and marked it **[TBC]**. Validation can only test against a specific number, so placeholder wording would leave them nothing to verify. The open items in Section 10 likely to have the biggest effect on the design are #5 (bag change versus the monotonic base totalizer) and #7 (how far QA's "any setpoint change" extends). Resolve those first.
